newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras sees A Band sell-off in mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Telebras sees A Band sell-off in mid-1998.

text.p: Brazil plans to begin privatizing its state-held A Band cellular frequency starting in July 1998, the head of Brazil's telecommunications giant Telebras said.

Telebras President Fernando Xavier told a Sao Paulo seminar that the federal telecoms behemoth will streamline and consolidate cellular functions of its 29 units as part of the overall preparation for privatization.
"We're going to put all our cellular functions in one area, so we will reach July 1998 fully prepared to be sold," he said.
The government in early 1997 will begin spinning off 10 concessions for its cellular B Band to private investors, with new operators beginning to provide services toward the end of next year.
The A Band will remain the domain of state firms until it too is opened to private capital starting in mid-1998, Xavier said.
Xavier said the emergence of private cellular providers will be more beneficial than harmful to the state-run Telebras system.
"More than a competitor, they will be an excellent customer of our," he added.
He acknowledged that poor cellular service, which first appeared locally three years ago, is the most frequent telecoms complaints in Brazil.
But, he added, that is due to problems the state monopoly has had keeping pace with explosive demand in what analysts predict will be one of the world's hottest cellular markets once privatized.
The B Band selloff will kick off the transfer of Brazil's mammoth federal telecoms sector - including Telecomunicacoes Brasileras SA, as Telebras is known formally - to private hands.
Xavier declined to discuss the details of the selloff process, saying Brazil's Communications Ministry is responsble for modeling the program, setting base prices and establishing schedules.
But, he added, Telebras is doing its part to prepare for the spin-off of its units, starting perhaps in 1998, by boosting investment, cutting its payroll and reducing expenses.
"We have our limitations but we know there's a lot of room to improve," Xavier said.
